summary: The clean-candidate check uses `git status --porcelain` and cannot see tracked files flagged skip-worktree or assume-unchanged, so a dirty worktree is minted as a clean immutable candidate identity.
failure_scenario: Tracked file F is committed, then edited on disk and flagged `git update-index --skip-worktree F` (or --assume-unchanged); verify_clean_tracked_candidate() returns a CandidateIdentityV1 for HEAD without error, while the qualify_* entry points (qualify_revoke_race, qualify_capacity_rollover, qualify_full_purge_cleanup, qualify_spool_crash_matrix, candidate_e2e_fast_track) run from that checkout and so execute bytes that differ from the identified HEAD tree.
evidence: Reproduced with stock git in a scratch repo: after commit, `echo dirty>f; git update-index --skip-worktree f` gave empty `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=no` output and empty `git diff HEAD --stat`, while `cat f` printed `dirty`. That is exactly the command _require_clean_tracked_state runs (lines 66-71), invoked before and after identity capture. The module was not run (pytest and the Windows modules are unavailable here), so the chain from the helper to the callers is read statically. candidate_source_archive_oracle._require_clean_checkout has the same blind spot, but the archive is built from git objects there, so the archive bytes are unaffected. No test covers index-flagged files.

summary: Run-journal state machine (qualification_run_journal._apply/_parse/_append) read in full: frame-then-head ordering, sealed-prefix-only application, genesis seeding from binding+location, strict canonical JSON, ordinal/state-transition guards and the poison-on-any-write-failure latch. No defect found. A torn tail beyond the committed head reads as integrity_complete=False and so as REFUSE_RETAINING; docs/adr/0002 and test_torn_corrupt_or_growing_input_is_never_recorded_complete accept that as the conservative design. Not reproduced at runtime because the I/O class is Windows-only.

qualification_recovery.acquire_recorded_root: intent -> launch -> bind -> resume_intent -> resume -> resumed ordering is fixed at a single call site, every raise path finalizes the owner, and _identity_of takes scenario and role from the owner's proof, not from the caller's intent, so the journal's process_bound comparison can still fire. disposition_of is a pure function that never resumes or claims absence. Sound (static read).

qualification_launch: the guardian/controller split, plan, launcher and kernel digest binding, sealed-resource declaration validation, and the unsettled-Job path (resources kept referenced, kill-on-close handle closed first, os._exit(2)) were read. The _RESOURCE_SOURCE_NAMES closure was checked with an ast walk over module-level imports from qualification_execution_files and qualification_file_seals: it covers every local module reached, with no extras and none missing apart from the package __init__, which is listed. A process created between _retain_cleanup_members and terminate_job is not individually awaited, which the code documents as an accepted limit. If its image teardown overlaps resources.close(), the observable result is a cleanup failure, not a false acceptance. Not exercised at runtime (Windows-only).

qualification_file_seals / qualification_execution_files: deny-write/delete share modes, identity re-check on exit, ancestry final-path binding, NTFS/fixed-volume requirement, frozen DACL applied through pre-opened control handles, namespace exact-set check, and cleanup that refuses to delete unless root identity still matches. No defect found; namespace protection is explicitly out of scope per the module docstring. Static read only.

qualification_tool_process._wait_for_tool_exit: reconciles live members against the cumulative Job TotalProcesses (a short-lived unobserved child refuses), requires TerminatedProcesses==0 and exit code 0 for every member, and re-checks the tool environment after finalization. Sound (static read).

candidate_source_archive_oracle capture path: identity is bound by full equality (captured != supplied), tree/blob objects are re-hashed against their OIDs, the archive is checked byte-for-byte against a regenerated canonical raw-tar header sequence, two archives must be equal, and Git metadata controls are sealed and revalidated around each Git run. Residual: repo-local config such as an include path is hashed but not parsed, so it could change Git output; any such change fails the closed equality/manifest checks, so I treat it as hardening and not a defect.

source_archive_authority.validated_archive_members and WindowsSourceWorkspaceAuthorityV1: prefix, case-fold collision, file-vs-directory, reserved-name and ADS-colon checks; exact shape/handle/digest equality in assert_unchanged. os.walk ignores errors, but the exact-shape comparison turns an unreadable directory into a refusal. No defect found.

qualification_candidate_files.bind_candidate_files: the input candidate document, source-role hashes and the archive reference are all compared to the verified archive metadata; wheels and sdists are verified from sealed bytes; the receipt re-checks the input digest, archive and wheels on every consumption. The role map is built with a dict comprehension, so a duplicate role in the document would silently take the last entry. Whether the document schema forbids duplicate roles lives in the retained_qualification_inputs/core validators, which are outside my slice, so I could not confirm it and report it as unresolved (missing witness: a duplicate-role input document and the schema it is validated against).

Prior claim scripts/task13_artifact_orchestrator.py:67 (git status cannot see skip-worktree / assume-unchanged): reproduced, reported above as the should-fix finding. It is the only prior claim whose target file is in this slice; the other prior claims are in other slices and were not assessed.

Limitation: pytest is not installed in this environment, so no repository tests were run. The Windows-only modules (journal I/O, launch, seals, execution files, tool process, Git child owner) cannot execute on this Linux host; those conclusions are static-read only. The git behaviour in the finding was reproduced with stock git.
